title: Choose the visual world
question: Piano Trainer's new colours and shape. Keep the assigned direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Chancel Glass
options.lineage: leaded stained-glass windows of the church the songs are sung in
options.thesis: The keyboard is a window: every musical meaning is one pane from a single set of glass, lit when it sounds.
materials: jewel glass panes, pale when unlit and full when lit
options.viewport: Laptop: the step or song fills a wide left column and the keyboard runs the full width below; phone: one column, the keyboard pinned at the thumb.
options.risk: Tips into church kitsch if lead outlines go everywhere; the leading stays hairline structure only.

raised.raise: One accent owns the chrome, committed: cobalt on every primary action, nothing else coloured outside the keys.
Every keyboard keeps one scale and one ground on every screen, like plates on one baseline.
One control opens the rest: each screen shows its few choices, one Options sheet holds the others.
Rest, sounding and held are three distinct key states, never a tint of one another.
Amber and red are reserved for a gap and a wrong key; no chrome carries a warning hue.

options.label: Ebony, Ivory and Felt
options.lineage: the upright piano itself: its keys, fallboard felt, brass and case
options.thesis: The app is made of the instrument: ivory keys, ebony type, the felt's wine as the one action.
options.viewport: Same wide layout; the keyboard reads as the piano's own keys under a felt-lined rail.
options.risk: The direction most piano apps land near: warm, familiar, at risk of old-fashioned.

options.label: Chord Specimen
options.thesis: The chord set like a specimen: huge on near-white paper, tiny labels, one accent.
options.viewport: The current chord at display size owns the top; the keyboard and choices sit small beneath.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on clarity (the chord read from the music stand); loses on audience, who do not know specimens.
options.risk: Austere; colour meaning on the keys has only one accent to live with.

options.label: Flash Scrawl Sleeve
options.viewport: A defaced photo with a scrawled logo.
options.case: Fuses poorly: church accompanists at the piano do not identify with club nights.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One plant through its seasons on fixed-scale plates.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a seasons metaphor does not carry chords and songs.
options.risk: Cream and engraving: the bookish rut.
options.kept: Every plate at the same scale and ground.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into shape.
options.viewport: A black semicircle gathered by one cord.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to the piano or the church.
options.risk: Dark and theatrical at a practice piano.
options.kept: One control that opens the rest.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Rods and red cord held in balance.
options.case: Fuses poorly: engineering labels read cold to a beginner.
options.kept: Slack, balanced and stressed states drawn distinctly.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.thesis: Six calm dials on a black panel.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a dark cockpit is not a daylit church hall.
options.kept: Caution colours used for caution only.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What piano-learning apps ship: white screens, one friendly brand blue, plain keys lit in that blue.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a learner expects from Flowkey or Simply Piano, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
